candidates.attacker_control: The XML document is the HTTP request entity. SourceProvider.readFrom (lines 45-50) hands the raw request InputStream to the application as a StreamSource without parsing it; whatever XML the attacker sends is later parsed by the writer whenever a resource returns a Source (echo/transform/proxy endpoints) or whenever a StreamSource built from attacker-controlled XML is written as a response entity. SourceProvider is an annotated built-in @Provider for text/xml, application/xml and application/*+xml.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that readFrom itself does not parse (so the vulnerability is specifically the write path) and that only StreamSource instances are re-wrapped/parsed here (DOMSource/SAXSource inputs are not re-parsed by this branch). Confirmed the project knows the XXE risk and hardens other XML providers by default (DocumentProvider lines 117-122, AbstractJAXBProvider default disableExternalEntities/disableDTDs, SecureUnmarshaller lines 344-352), which shows intent but no guard in SourceProvider. Confirmed the class is a default @Provider for XML media types and is exercised by testsuite resources that return StreamSource (testsuite/integration-tests/.../sourceProvider/resource/BookResource.java line 45). Considered that an application could itself parse/transform the XML before returning it (then the flaw would already be in application code); the library-side parse at line 81/85 still occurs whenever the returned entity is a StreamSource. No runtime test or scanner was run, so exploitability was not executed.
candidates.impact: Server-side XXE: disclosure of local files readable by the application process (configuration, credentials, /etc/passwd-style files), SSRF against reachable internal HTTP/file resources, and denial of service via recursive entity expansion (billion-laughs style) because secure processing / entity limits are also not enabled. Affects confidentiality, integrity and availability of the server hosting the JAX-RS application.
candidates.prerequisites: A deployed JAX-RS application with a resource method whose response entity is a javax.xml.transform.Source (StreamSource), typically built from the request XML (for example an endpoint that accepts Source and returns it, or returns a StreamSource over attacker-supplied data). Attacker must be able to reach that endpoint and supply a body containing a DOCTYPE with an external general/parameter entity. No special configuration is needed; the provider is registered by default for XML media types.
candidates.root_cause: SourceProvider.writeTo() wraps any StreamSource in a SAXSource built from SAXParserFactory.newInstance().newSAXParser().getXMLReader() (line 81) with no DTD/entity/external-access restrictions, then runs a default TransformerFactory identity transform (line 85) that parses the document and resolves external entities. The same module hardens every other XML entry point (DocumentProvider sets FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, disallow-doctype-decl, external-general-entities/external-parameter-entities at lines 117-122; JAXB SecureUnmarshaller.configureParserFactory sets the same features at lines 344-352), so SourceProvider is the unprotected outlier.
candidates.title: XXE in default Source message-body writer (SourceProvider) due to unhardened SAXParserFactory
candidates.trace: POST XML body -> SourceProvider.readFrom returns StreamSource over the raw entity stream (no parse) -> resource method receives/derives the Source and returns it as the response entity -> ServerResponseWriter selects SourceProvider for type Source -> SourceProvider.writeTo wraps the StreamSource in a SAXSource using a default SAXParserFactory XMLReader (line 81) -> TransformerFactory.newInstance().newTransformer().transform(source, result) (line 85) parses the document -> the default JAXP/Xerces parser permits DOCTYPE and resolves external entities, so file:// or http(s):// entity content (or entity-expansion output) is emitted into the response body.
candidates.unverified: No runtime confirmation. The exact CVE/JIRA mapping could not be derived from repository content. The candidate relies on the standard JDK/JAXP default behaviour (DOCTYPE allowed, external-general-entities/external-parameter-entities enabled, FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING off) of whichever SAXParserFactory implementation is on the deployment classpath; that behaviour was not executed or verified here. It is also unverified whether a typical consuming application pre-parses the XML (which would already expand entities outside RESTEasy) and whether any deployment-layer EntityResolver/security manager changes the parser defaults.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE)

coverage_summary: Scope: 4285 source-root files (4284 model-visible; one path/name excluded by the safety filters; no binaries included). P1 index coverage is partial: 3870 Java files parsed (102 omitted), 32317 symbols, 94865 call candidates, 73997 unresolved calls, and no data-flow/control-flow or semantic resolution; Spring/DI and security enforcement are annotation-name hints only. I used the index for navigation (symbol lookups, security_call/test/config facts) and verified every referenced element in source text. Files inspected in depth: resteasy-core providers (SourceProvider, DocumentProvider), JAXB providers (SecureUnmarshaller, AbstractJAXBProvider, JAXBElementProvider, JAXBXmlTypeProvider, Collection/Map providers), ExceptionHandler, SynchronousDispatcher, ResourceMethodRegistry/registry nodes, StringParameterInjector and Query/Path/Matrix injectors, MessageSanitizerContainerResponseFilter and its unit/integration tests, ConfigurationBootstrap/ResteasyContextParameters/ResteasyDeploymentImpl/RegisterBuiltin, client engines (ManualClosingApacheHttpClient43Engine, ApacheHttpClient43Engine, URLConnectionEngine, ClientHttpEngineBuilder43, JettyClientEngine, ReactorNetty engine), jsapi/wadl servlets, security/jose-jwt and security/resteasy-crypto interceptors, plus relevant testsuite unit/integration tests (sourceProvider, xxe, html sanitizer, redirect, basic auth). Broad text searches were run for XML parser factories, ObjectInputStream/readObject, Runtime.exec/ProcessBuilder, path handling (getRealPath/new File), TrustManager, Authorization, followRedirect/redirect, CVE and sanitizer/XSS markers across all 4284 visible files. Not exhaustively reviewed: most server adapters, CDI/Spring/Guice wiring, wadl generation internals, cache module, and the large testsuite (used as context only).
limitations: No code was executed, no exploit payloads were run, and no runtime/container behaviour was observed; findings are source-level only and the candidate is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.

The P1 relation index explicitly lacks control-flow, data-flow and semantic resolution; its call/inheritance edges are name-based candidates and 102 files are omitted, so reachability of SourceProvider.writeTo in any particular application was reasoned from source annotations, not proven.

Behaviour of dependency jars not present in the snapshot (JAXP/Xerces default entity resolution, Apache HttpClient redirect header handling, JDK HttpURLConnection redirect/credential behaviour) was assumed from general knowledge and could not be verified against this snapshot.
No repository content ties this snapshot or the candidate to a specific CVE/JIRA; the dataset case-to-CVE mapping could not be confirmed from source.
Some areas (server adapters, CDI/Spring/Guice, cache, wadl generation, large testsuite) were only spot-checked, so additional issues may exist outside the inspected paths.

rejected_leads.lead: Reflected XSS gap: MessageSanitizerContainerResponseFilter escapes HTML only for status 400 (lines 43-52), while ExceptionHandler returns attacker-influenced messages as text/html for 404 (handleClientErrorException lines 222-261) and for other Failure codes (handleFailure lines 204-221). StringParameterInjector passes raw decoded values into those messages on the paramConverter/unmarshaller/header-delegate paths (lines 685-709), and query/path/matrix injectors convert the resulting BadRequestException into a 404.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible but weaker/conditional: it needs an application with a failing custom ParamConverter/StringParameterUnmarshaller/HeaderDelegate (built-in primitive/enum failures URL-encode the value via _encode), and it depends on browser rendering of the decoded value; I could not verify from this snapshot that the corresponding upstream fix targeted this code, so it was not selected as the single candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Client credential/header handling on redirects: ManualClosingApacheHttpClient43Engine.setRedirectRequired enables redirects without stripping sensitive headers (lines 684-689), and URLConnectionEngine unconditionally follows GET redirects (line 198).
rejected_leads.reason: No in-snapshot evidence of the actual header-copy behaviour: whether Authorization/credentials are forwarded cross-host is decided inside Apache HttpClient and the JDK HttpURLConnection, which are dependency jars not present in the snapshot. Opt-in redirects (followRedirects defaults to false, documented at docbook/resteasy ... RESTEasy_Client_Framework.xml lines 694-706) further narrow it. Could not be verified to source level.

rejected_leads.lead: SerializableProvider uses ObjectInputStream for request bodies (resteasy-core/.../SerializableProvider.java around line 113).
rejected_leads.reason: Documented as disabled by default and only enabled explicitly by the application via META-INF/services or provider registration (class Javadoc lines 31-40); not a vulnerability in the default configuration.

rejected_leads.lead: RoleBasedSecurityFilter grants access when no SecurityContext is present in ResteasyContext (lines 41-53).
rejected_leads.reason: All in-repo server adapters examined push a SecurityContext per request (ServletContainerDispatcher line 244, netty/vertx RequestDispatcher, jdk-http BasicAuthFilter), so the null-context path does not appear reachable in the shipped adapters; left unconfirmed rather than reported.

summary: Defensive source review of the RESTEasy snapshot (4.6.0-SNAPSHOT, javax.* line). I surveyed the whole tree by path listing and text search, then focused on XML/parsing providers, exception/error rendering, message sanitization, parameter injection, client engines and security modules, using the P1 relation index only for navigation and verifying everything against source text. The strongest source-evidenced issue is an unhardened XML parse in the default Source message-body writer (SourceProvider.writeTo), which can expose JAX-RS applications that return a javax.xml.transform.Source derived from untrusted XML to XXE (file disclosure / SSRF / entity-expansion DoS). A second plausible but weaker lead — the reflected-XSS gap where MessageSanitizerContainerResponseFilter only escapes status 400 while ExceptionHandler returns attacker-influenced text/html messages for 404 and other failures — is recorded as a rejected (unconfirmed) lead, not a second candidate. No runtime confirmation was performed.
